profile_headline: Data Scientist @Walmart Labs India || Google Developer Expert ML || Indian Statistical Institute
post_content:
Many a times, while using a loss function in supervised learning tasks, we
tend to forget certain very important mathematical properties and assumptions
of the same. Have you ever given a thought on what will happen if we use Mean
Squared Error instead of LogLoss in case of Logistic regression given that it
is called regression. Our blog (mine and Rajesh Shreedhar Bhat) 'Why not Mean
Squared Error(MSE) as a loss function for Logistic Regression' shows that why
log loss is recommended for Logistic regression using mathematical
justifications considering the convexity and penalising aspects of both the
loss functions. It has been published in Towards Data Science (Online
Publication).Would be happy to hear your comments/feedback on the same and
feel free to click on 👏 if you like the content of the blog.
